published_source: Authors' Stata log (Table1,3,4,5,7.log, esttab output re-run by the authors on the shipped data); no article text or PDF in the project.
data_provenance: real (anonymized: README says identifiers and some variables were modified to protect proprietary information while preserving consistency; not synthetic; the shipped data reproduce the authors' logs exactly)
replication_status: exact (fixest reproduces the authors' log coefficient, SE and N; published article not available to compare)
notes: CONTROLS ANALYSIS (PROTOCOL 5c). Authors: reghdfe ltotal_order_amount_byorder did beauty_num culture_num transport_num cafe_num housing_num mart_num medical_num, absorb(date1 newid) vce(cluster newid) on Data/Table1_dateset.dta. did = subscribe x post; post switches on at the user's own subscription date (absorbing, no switch-offs); 1:1 matched sample of subscribers and never-subscribers (matching on Jan-Jul 2019 user means; PROTOCOL 5b: matched sample = sample restriction). Only violation: seven daily category transaction counts as time-varying controls, entered linearly. Unit = user (newid), time = day (date_num = days since 1970-01-01), user and date FE, no weights, clustered by user. Balanced user-day panel, 2,162 users x 396 days (2019-01-01 to 2020-01-31); 137 daily adoption cohorts (2019-08-01 to 2020-01-28); 50 percent never-treated; no always-treated. gvar g_date = first day with post = 1. Outcome defined only on days with at least one order (per-order amount), so the sample is selected on the outcome margin and highly unbalanced. DEVIATIONS: none for TWFE (singletons kept by run_spec; reghdfe drops them, which leaves the coefficient unchanged). CSA on the daily panel is expected to hit the size guard (up to 137 daily cohorts x 396 days).
